::: {.project-detail}

::: {.project-hook}
What changes when a financial-information interface begins in the user’s language rather than asking the user to adapt to English?
:::

## What I built

I developed and deployed a multilingual proof of concept that lets users ask financial questions through web and Telegram interfaces, using both voice and text. Instead of treating deployment as the finish line, I also built a protected analytics view to compare interaction patterns across languages and modalities.

- Designed a multilingual frontend and backend service
- Created Telegram and web interaction paths
- Supported voice and text input across local-language interactions
- Added authentication and protected user metrics
- Deployed cloud infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code
- Built an analytics dashboard comparing language and modality patterns

![](/assets/projects/vernacular-chatbot/thumbnail.png){.project-screenshot fig-alt="Vernacular chatbot interface"}

## Research problem behind the prototype

The prototype grew from time spent alongside researchers exploring a larger question: how might AI make reliable financial information more accessible to rural and suburban customers who communicate most naturally in local languages?

[Project SATHI](https://gcgh.grandchallenges.org/grant/enabling-equal-finance-access-rural-customers-india){target="_blank"} is an IISc-led institutional initiative designed around that challenge. Its published description combines information about government financial schemes with translation, local-language voice queries, audio responses, and field testing. The project brought together IISc researchers and collaborators including Oxford Brookes University, Akaike, and Kotak Mahindra Bank.

That institutional initiative provided the research context—not a title or grant affiliation for me. I was not a named member of the core team or a participant in the grant. My contribution was the independently implemented proof of concept presented here. The Grand Challenges funding supported the institutional project, not my personal work.

## Process desk

::: {.process-desk}
::: {.process-card}
<span>01 · Prototype</span>

**Conversation flow**

The interface began with a deliberately narrow question: can a user ask a financial question in a familiar language and receive an accessible response without first adapting to an English-only workflow?
:::

::: {.process-card}
<span>02 · Infrastructure</span>

**From local code to cloud deployment**

The implementation evolved from a local conversation flow into authenticated services, serverless deployment, infrastructure-as-code, protected webhooks, and two interaction channels.
:::

::: {.process-card}
<span>03 · Observe</span>

**Usage dashboard**

The deployed dashboard makes language and voice-versus-text patterns visible, turning a working interface into something that could also support observation and iteration.
:::
:::
